subject: Promo credit issuance — suspicious signup signals from ProofPoint Labs
messages:
From: Oliver Sand <oliver@proofpoint.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@proofpoint.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T09:15:00Z
Subject: Promo credit request — duplicates in self-serve grant

Hi Markus + Monica,

We saw several of our engineers sign up via the self-serve flow but only a subset received the promotional credits shown in your docs. Attached is a small audit (signup-audit.csv) and a capture of session headers (session-headers.txt) showing multiple attempts from the same fingerprint and a suspiciously high success rate for disposable emails.

Key points:
- ~12 signups from the same device fingerprint over 48 hours.
- Two emails tied to the same device but different email providers (one company alias + personal gmail).
- No payment method added; we were expecting credits for onboarding activity.

Can you confirm whether these accounts were auto-approved for the promo grant? We can share more logs if helpful. We don't want to appear to be trying to game free credits, but the pattern looks odd and we want to ensure the grant was used legitimately before we commit to more licenses.

Attached: signup-audit.csv, session-headers.txt

Thanks — Oliver
ProofPoint Labs

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — duplicates in self-serve grant

Monica / Ben / Priya,

Looping you in — Oliver from ProofPoint flagged a cluster of signups that may indicate either: duplicate accounts linked to one org contact, or automated signups attempting to claim promo credits. I think we should triage before approving any additional top-ups for DL-77821.

Immediate asks:
- Monica: can you run a quick provenance check (device fingerprint, IP churn, cookie replay) against SEC-4521 and confirm whether the signals match our bot heuristics? Use the attached session-headers.txt.
- Ben: pause any manual credit top-ups to this account until we confirm. If the initial credits were already applied, flag them for hold so CS doesn't auto-renew.
- Priya: prep a conservative reply template for the account team that offers a limited test grant and asks for org verification documents (company domain verification / invoice contact).

Let's keep this tight — if it's legit we want to restore service quickly; if not, we need to avoid giving away credits to automated flows.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — duplicates in self-serve grant

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:02, Markus Klein wrote:
> Monica / Ben / Priya,
>
> Looping you in — Oliver from ProofPoint flagged a cluster of signups that may indicate either: duplicate accounts linked to one org contact, or automated signups attempting to claim promo credits. I think we should triage before approving any additional top-ups for DL-77821.

Quick triage results (summary):
- Device fingerprint: consistent across 11 of 12 signups (same UA, same canvas hash).
- IPs: three distinct IPs within the same ASN, rapid rotation consistent with a residential proxy set.
- Email patterns: one canonical company alias (oliver.sand@proofpoint.ai) plus multiple variations using +aliasing and disposable domains.
- Session headers (see session-headers.txt): repeated Authorization and X-Request-Id patterns that suggest session replay / captured cookies.

Recommendation:
1) DO NOT issue full promo top-up.
2) Apply a small verification grant (25% of requested credits) to enable their engineers to proceed with a short proof-of-value.
3) Ask ProofPoint to: confirm a named billing contact, share an invoice or PO, or complete the org verification form.
4) If they provide evidence within 7 days, we can release remainder and lift the hold.

I can package the technical summary for their security team — should I send it directly to security@proofpoint.ai and Oliver? Also uploaded a short Doc (doc-signature-proposal.pdf) with a suggested verification checklist.

- Monica
Sr. Trust & Safety Analyst
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Sand <oliver@proofpoint.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, billing@proofpoint.ai
Date: 2027-04-03T17:42:00Z
Subject: Decision on promo credits for ProofPoint Labs (DL-77821)

Hi Oliver — thanks for flagging and for the data you sent. Monica ran a quick provenance check and found multiple indicators consistent with session replay and proxy churn rather than independent human signups.

To balance security with friction for legitimate onboarding, here's what we'll do immediately:
- Hold additional manual credit issuance for DL-77821 until verification completes.
- We will issue a limited verification grant: 25% of the standard promo credits, applied today to the verified email oliver.sand@proofpoint.ai.
- To unlock the remainder, please provide one of the following within 7 days:
  * Signed PO or invoice showing company purchase intent, or
  * Confirmation from your billing contact (billing@proofpoint.ai) plus a short video (screen capture) of an admin confirming org ownership, or
  * Completion of our org verification form (link below).

If you want the technical summary Monica prepared, we can send it to security@proofpoint.ai — it contains the session header captures and a short list of fields we flagged.

DocuSign for verification: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/DL-77821/verify
Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4521
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/77821

We appreciate ProofPoint wanting to move quickly — we can escalate if you can provide verification sooner. If you prefer, Ben can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the steps.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations
